old_snapshot_survives_compaction: a pre-compaction snapshot returns identical data after compaction and after a further commit; compaction bumps commit_seq by 1 and keeps logical contents.
second_open_locked: a second writable open and a read-only open of a locked FaultVfs path both give 55006; after close the open succeeds.
assumptions: Executor::step(WorkOp::Compact) returns StepOutcome::Crashed when the disk crashes mid-compaction, and Done on success.
FaultController::log() records mutating_index and OpKind::Rename/SyncDir when plan.record_log is set.
Compaction performs exactly one rename and a sync_dir after it, per the STO-17 protocol; the Drop/Keep assertions depend on that.
Dropping the last Container clone releases the FaultFile lock.
Container::verify and OpenOptions.verify = Full report no errors on valid containers; the export destination opens with default read-write options.
Executor::step Put/Commit works after a compaction, and the model's acked state is kept across it.
TreeSnapshot::scan on PageId::NONE yields an empty iterator.

implemented_behaviors: verify_tree: explicit-stack DFS with (lo, hi) key bounds inherited per child; per-tree seen set (duplicate reference -> Error 'referenced twice'); global seen set (shared subtrees checked once); leaf/internal parsing via leaf_spans/internal_spans; uniform-depth level check; height = root level + 1; key length, node capacity, separator ordering and bounds checks; overflow chains via chain_pages with 'could be inline' Warning; empty-leaf Warnings; corruption becomes Error with named page (from message/detail), other errors abort with Err

verify_snapshot: Level None checks superblock fields only (directory root beyond page_count -> Error); Roots reads directory root and every collect_roots root page via decode_node; Full runs verify_tree on directory and all roots, trace(per_root=true) for kinds/roots, reachable/unreachable counts from the verify ReachSet, and a garbage scan via read_page_uncached emitting only Info 'unreachable page <id> does not verify (garbage)'
verify_container: verify_snapshot plus slots and recovery from recovery_report

verify_file: vfs.open ReadOnly, shared try_lock (WouldBlock -> 55006), read_slots, choose_slot failure -> Ok report with one Error issue; otherwise drop handle and Container::open_with read-only with verify None, corruption on open -> Ok report with Error issue; other errors propagate

Unit tests: healthy container verifies clean and JSON parses; flipped byte in reachable page -> Error naming that page; flipped byte in superseded directory root -> only Info; garbage file -> Ok report with Error; named-page extraction and half-open key bounds
assumptions: verify_file on a missing path returns Err 58P01 (open_failed) rather than a report, since that is a non-corruption open failure; the contract only mandates a report for the choose_slot failure.
verify_file converts XX001 errors from Container::open_with into an Ok report with one Error issue instead of Err, consistent with 'doctor reports corruption as Issues'.
collect_roots lists the directory entry first when the directory root is non-NONE; verify_roots and verify_full rely on that to skip index 0 (the directory is verified separately).
Shared subtrees across trees are skipped once globally seen, so a corrupt shared subtree is reported only under the first tree that reaches it, per the lease's 'checked once' rule.

In verify_full, if trace() fails with corruption and no Error issue exists yet, an Error 'reachability trace failed' with no page is added; otherwise trace corruption is silent because verify_tree already reported it.
pages_checked counts nodes and overflow pages visited by verify_tree (not garbage pages that happen to verify).
contract_breaks: PgError carries no page id, so corruption errors from chain_pages and similar calls are attributed to a page by parsing the message ('invalid page in block N', 'page reference N') or detail ('page N of database file'); unnamed errors fall back to the parent page. A structured page field on corruption errors would make this exact.
